name: Zercher Squat
description: The Zercher squat is performed with the barbell cradled in the crooks of the elbows at the front of the torso, requiring a very upright posture and strong isometric bicep and upper back engagement. This unusual loading position keeps the center of mass close to the body, promotes a deep, upright squat, and places significant demand on the core. It is an effective alternative for those with shoulder limitations that prevent front or back rack positions.

execution.starting_position: Set the barbell in a rack at mid-torso height. Squat under the bar and position it in the crooks of your elbows by bending your arms to 90°. Clasp your hands together in front. Stand to unrack, then step back.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the safety bars at a height allowing you to get the bar into your elbow crooks easily. Padding on the bar or wearing long sleeves reduces discomfort on the forearms and inner elbows.
steps: Step 1: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed out, holding the bar in your elbow crooks with arms bent and clasped together.
Step 2: Brace your core hard and keep your chest tall as you initiate the squat by simultaneously pushing the knees out and sitting the hips down.
Step 3: Descend to at least parallel or as deep as mobility allows while keeping the torso upright.
Step 4: Drive through the full foot to return to standing. Keep the elbows elevated throughout to prevent the bar from dropping.
Step 5: Exhale at the top and reset the brace before the next repetition.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before the descent. Hold through the squat. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Allowing the elbows to drop, which causes the torso to pitch forward
Rounding the upper back under the load
Using excessively heavy weight before adapting to the discomfort of the bar on the arms
safety_considerations: The bar can be dropped forward in a failed rep — use bumper plates when training alone
Start with light weight to acclimate to the bar position on the forearms
Elbow padding or a bar pad reduces bruising during adaptation
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Aim for parallel or below while maintaining an upright torso without lumbar rounding.
coaching_cues: Keep your elbows pointing forward — don't let them drop to your sides
Chest up, sit between your knees
Drive through your heels and midfoot equally
